newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL LOOK TO TAKE STEP TOWARDS TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL LOOK TO TAKE STEP TOWARDS TITLE.

text.p: Unbeaten Liverpool will be seeking to take a major step towards their first title since 1990 by becoming the first team to beat Manchester United at home in the league for nearly two years on Saturday morning.
United have not lost a home league match since December 17, 1994 when Nottingham Forest beat them 2-1 and, since then, they have played 35 home league games, winning 24 and drawing 11.

Because of the unusual kickoff time -- the result of the match being shown live on satellite television -- both sides will be changing their usual pre-match preparations but that has not worried Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson too much,
"It suits us," he said on Friday, "because it gives us more time to recover for next week's champions' league match against Feberbahce in Turkey."
Ferguson was waiting to check on the fitness of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Karel Poborksy, who played World Cup matches for Norway and the Czech Republic this week.
But he is keen to put out his strongest available side for a match that, even this early in the season, could have a major bearing on the outcome of the title race.
Liverpool are four points clear of fourth-placed United and Ferguson admits it is vital his side do not lose on Saturday.
"There will be a lot of tension, a lot of passion," he said.
"There is great rivalry with the fans so the atmosphere is guaranteed. With Liverpool being clear it means we have to do well because we don't want them to stretch their lead."

Manchester United will be looking to Solskjaer to continue his wonderful start in their colours. The young Norwegian has scored five times for United in eight appearances -- four of those as substitute -- and has scored on all four occasions he has played at Old Trafford.

Liverpool have not lost a competitive match since United beat them 1-0 in the F.A. Cup final last May and are looking for their eighth successive win on Saturday -- and their first at Old Trafford since 1990.
One man particularly keen to erase the memory of the Cup Final is Liverpool goalkeeper David James, who has recently been in outstanding form.

But it was his ill-judged leap and mistimed punch from a corner with just four minutes remaining at Wembley that presented Eric Cantona with a chance to score the only goal of the game -- and wrap up United's second League and Cup double in three seasons.
James said this week: "Don't remind me of that. I've thought about it ever since and it's not something I've enjoyed.
"I wasn't happy with my contribution and we lost. But this is another day and another chance."
"The worst thing was that it was the last game of the season, the one everybody remembers and the one you spend all summer thinking about when you're on holiday."
It was in this same fixture last year that Cantona returned to soccer following his eight-month ban for attacking a fan -- and he marked it by scoring a penalty in a 2-2 draw.

Robbie Fowler scored both Liverpool goals but injury may keep him out on Saturday. Liverpool defender Dominic Matteo, who had to withdraw from the England squad in midweek because of an injury, looks like he may be fit enough to play.
United will be missing broken leg-victim Andy Cole as well as Roy Keane and Phil Neville.

But manager Ferguson has been heartened by the news that central defender Ronny Johnsen returned to action in Norway's World Cup qualifying victory over Hungary on Wednesday night after recovering from the ankle knock he picked up two weeks ago.
Teams:

Manchester United (from): 1-Peter Schmeichel; 2-Gary Neville, 6-Gary Pallister, 4-David May, 19-Ronnie Johnsen, 3-Denis Irwin; 10-David Beckham, 7-Eric Cantona, 8-Nicky Butt, 11-Ryan Giggs; 15-Karel Poborsky, 20-Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, 13-Brian McClair, 18-Paul Scholes.

Liverpool (from): 1-David James; 3-John Scales, 14-Neil Ruddock, 4-Jason McAteer, 21-Dominic Matteo, 6-Phil Babb; 7-Steve McManaman, 8-Stan Collymore, 16-Michael Thomas; 9-Robbie Fowler, 11-Jamie Redknapp, 10-John Barnes, 15-Patrik Berger, 24-Lee Jones.
Referee: David Elleray
